environment.atspi: AT-SPI 2.60.6; native Wayland Qt QPA; isolated session D-Bus and registry
environment.assistive_technology: Orca and Accerciser are not installed; a small public AT-SPI client was used, not a screen reader.
environment.scope: Research-only public AT-SPI probe and loopback fixture; no production provider or behavior change.
environment.desktop_state: Both live AT-SPI status flags and both GNOME accessibility preferences were false after the isolated probe; the probe checks private-bus addressing and the desktop preferences.

baseline_comparison: Based on S23's recorded evidence commit af0e484. S24 adds an opt-in public AT-SPI client probe, QML test, and synthetic loopback fixture; browser production code and defaults are unchanged.

observations: The existing cross-origin and closed-root WebEngine cases passed; semantic access remains limited to the parent-visible surface.
The engine gate passed 442 engine-crate tests, 144 QML/WebEngine tests, and native CTest 1/1.

test_results.reason: No native keyboard journey was sent: the nested Weston path lacks the virtual-keyboard protocol required by wtype, as recorded in the existing S23 qualification.

test_results.command: pkg-config --modversion Qt6Core Qt6WebEngineCore atspi-2; inspect public Qt accessibility documentation and local tool availability
observations: The probe uses public AT-SPI and documented Qt environment/API routes only; Orca and Accerciser are absent.
The public QML button exposed its name, button role, and Press action; the action ran once and its destroyed object became defunct, left the tree, and rejected a stale press.

The QML button had no component bounds. The loaded WebEngine document exposed an unnamed document node with no button, canvas, or closed-root child semantics, so the provider capability result is no-go.
The run used native Wayland and a private AT-SPI session; it did not test a real screen reader.

scope_amendments: Added crates/ferric-browser-engine-qt/tests/accessibility-probes/ as an isolated, opt-in S24 module for the AT-SPI client and QML probe. The synthetic HTML fixture remains under the canonical tests/fixtures/webapp-interaction/ root. No production source or page-side instrumentation was added.
remaining_risks: Orca and Accerciser are unavailable, so spoken output, focus/navigation announcements, and real screen-reader coexistence remain unqualified.
The WebEngine child-tree absence and QML bounds result are specific to the tested Qt 6.11.2 Wayland configuration; they do not establish universal Qt or platform behavior.
No production semantic provider is enabled; the existing visual Grid fallback remains the supported interaction path.
Qt versions below the declared 6.11.2 package minimum were not tested.
not_run_reasons: T035/native-wayland: nested Weston does not provide the virtual-keyboard protocol required by wtype; native keyboard input remains unqualified.
T051/real-screen-reader: Orca and Accerciser are not installed; the custom AT-SPI client probe cannot establish screen-reader coexistence.
